layout_why: The product promises one action this week, so each page is a numbered read-your-bill walkthrough, not a dashboard clone.
navigation_why: 2000 tariffs need state -> utility -> schedule depth for crawl paths and contextual linking; a flat top bar collapses at this size.
visual_why: Meters, demand curves and load shapes are engineering objects; drafting lines signal measurement and avoid generic SaaS purple.

type_pairing.reason: Archivo has tabular figures for charge tables; Newsreader stays readable for older owners on phones. Two faces only, numerals via font-variant-numeric, no third mono download.

motion_why: All-age audience; 120ms state changes only, full prefers-reduced-motion bypass.

imagery_strategy.photo_style: macro/documentary of physical utility hardware: meter dials, service panels, gas risers, rooftop condensers
imagery_strategy.treatment: cyanotype duotone at 18% over grayscale, 2px hard ink frame, no rounded corners
imagery_strategy.svg_first_rule: LINE_ITEM and PLAN_PATTERN pages get generated blueprint SVG heroes (waveform, load shape, charge stack). A photo of a random meter adds nothing to 'what is a therm'. Photos are reserved for RATE_SCHEDULE and UTILITY_HUB pages where a real object exists. This is a deliberate deviation from photo-on-every-page; flagging it rather than hiding it.
imagery_strategy.exclusions: no faces, no readable brand logos, no before/after savings imagery
